newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close sharply up on Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close sharply up on Q1 results.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed sharply higher on Friday on the back of sustained buying interest in blue chip and secondary counters after some companies announced positive first quarter earnings, brokers said.

The Jakarta composite index closed 6.85 points, or 1.03 percent, higher at a day high of 673.69 points. Advancers led decliners by 75 to 52, with 57 counters unchanged. Total turnover was estimated at 524.7 trillion rupiah on a volume of 245.96 million shares.
For the week, the index has risen 25.80 points, or about four percent.
"Overall market sentiment was firm today. It seems everybody wants to buy, especially in issues belonging to the Lippo Group," one broker said.
She added that announcement of sound first quarter results of companies such as Lippo Life and Lippo Securities had prompted the buying.
Reports that Hari Darmawan, founder of Matahari Putra Prima, planned to add to his current 10 percent stake in Lippo's retail unit Multipolar also boosted the group's counter, brokers said.
Buying interest in blue chip Bank Negara Indonesia was also high after it announced first quarter results which brokers said were in line with market expectations.

"Actually active buying on BNI and Lippo group units started on Wednesday but some buyers had to carry over their buying order to Friday as the market was closed on Thursday," a broker with a local firm said.

The sharp rise in the Dow Jones overnight also provided a boost and prompted foreign buying in blue chip counters such as Telkom, cigarette maker Gudang Garam and toll road operator Citra Marga, brokers said.
Telkom closed 150 rupiah higher at 3,850 rupiah with some 9.1 million shares traded.
Brokers said the rise was linked to reports that it had formally set up a multimedia joint venture which will start operations in 1998.
Property firm Elang Realty, which now has changed its name to Bakrie Land Development, was the most active stock.
It rose 25 rupiah to 1,675 rupiah with some 35.6 million shares traded on news that it got shareholder approval for a rights issue this year, brokers said.
